verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: CPS Release 2 defines CPM generation and object inclusion rules, including Value-of-Information filtering and bounded omission before re-inclusion.
CAM generation is event-driven within bounded intervals and coupled to DCC behavior.
DENM lifecycle semantics distinguish update, repetition, original-sender cancellation, other-station negation, and validity expiry using actionID-scoped state.
The official work item defines concepts and messages for coordinated maneuvers; the stable draft status shown was 0.0.10 dated 2025-02-17.
The official analysis work item covers cooperative maneuver coordination use cases and requirements.
CPMs have variable interval and size; senders may apply inclusion rules and need not place all perceived objects in one CPM.
ETSI documents an ITS conformance-validation framework and the relation between interoperability and conformance testing.
The event exercised CAM and DENM interoperability and TTCN-3 conformance suites.
The official report records C-V2X interoperability and conformance activity rather than planner-level maneuver outcomes.
ETSI publishes official CPM ASN.1 modules under a BSD-3-Clause license.
The official DENM ASN.1 history exposes the termination enumeration used for cancellation and negation.
The official test-suite repository includes CAM and DENM ATS paths built with TITAN and Docker.
The specification defines service requirements for enhanced V2X scenarios.
The study covers enhanced 5G V2X support and cooperative-driving use cases.
The specification defines V2X application-layer support architecture and information flows.
The specification defines 5GS architectural enhancements for V2X services.
The Stage-3 specification defines V2X service signalling in 5GS; it does not itself define an ETSI or SAE maneuver proposition rollback object.
The taxonomy distinguishes state-sharing, intent-sharing, agreement-seeking, and prescriptive cooperation classes.
The standard defines application protocol requirements for maneuver sharing and coordinating services.
The standard defines Sensor Sharing Service message flow, entities, and object information for cooperative automation.
A proving-ground MCM prototype connects negotiation to a real deceleration and gap-creation action in cut-in scenarios.
A distributed maneuver-coordination protocol uses agreement to prevent conflicting maneuver changes and evaluates communication failures.
AutoMCM includes advertisement, intention, prescription, acceptance, finalization, cancellation, acknowledgement, and timeout behavior.
The study identifies cooperative-maneuver failure causes and evaluates mitigations including retransmission under packet loss.
The work implements a complete maneuver-cancellation state machine, message set, repeated delivery, completion confirmation, timeout logic, and mobility recovery.
Adaptive message-generation rules for maneuver-coordination services directly occupy a message-frequency candidate family.
The protocol bounds disagreement under asymmetric packet loss and defines cooperative versus autonomous fallback modes.
Collective-perception generation is analyzed from tracking-accuracy, update-age, and safety perspectives.
VILE explicitly studies the case where an object is omitted because a prior CPM is presumed received although it was lost.
The study evaluates CPM generation rules against object-tracking accuracy, providing a direct functional baseline.
The study develops data-compression and segmentation mechanisms for cooperative perception messages, providing a direct protocol-level baseline for variable object-set transmission.
NIST publishes C-V2V, C-V2I, and C-V2X PCAP or PDML interoperability captures for IEEE 1609 and SAE J2735; the catalog does not provide maneuver commitments or planner outcomes.
Vanetza provides an open ETSI ITS protocol stack, ASN.1 codecs, and CPM test vectors.
VaN3Twin is an official public V2X digital-twin simulation asset, but the complete path is not a lightweight parser-only dependency.
OpenC2X publishes a standalone open V2X stack; the fixed official commit is old and does not expose an MCM-to-planner path.
CommonRoad-IO provides executable planning-scenario parsing but no official ETSI or SAE protocol-state bridge.
CommonRoad provides public motion-planning scenarios and tools suitable only after a justified protocol-to-planner mapping exists.
The VaN3Twin paper documents the integrated V2X digital-twin simulation architecture and its full-stack dependencies.

conclusion.summary: No candidate survived both required gates: a natural protocol event in a public asset and an actual planning or safety consequence not already occupied by direct protocol work or ordinary standards engineering. MCM revision, cancellation, commitment breach, and reconnect ideas collide with current v9 rejects and direct state-machine priors. DENM semantics are normative but lack public planner consequences. CPM omission and variable object-set behavior are real but currently terminate at tracking or network effects and would revive excluded fusion, AoI, or schema work. Public interoperability traces expose packets but not maneuver commitments and actions.
decisiveEvidence: The fixed Vanetza commit passed a real CPM UPER decode and byte-identical re-encode, satisfying the lightweight execution gate without being promoted to occurrence or task evidence.
Six official repository commits were fixed and checked; no official asset joined protocol lifecycle, natural event, and planner outcome in one executable path.
NIST interoperability artifacts are public and concrete but carry IEEE 1609 or SAE J2735 packet evidence rather than maneuver-state and planner labels.
The strongest natural protocol mechanism found was CPM object omission; direct redundancy and tracking work already covers it, and no verified actual planning consequence remains.
